title: Confidence-Faithfulness Gap Meter: Does Stated Confidence Match Reasoning?

original_idea.body: Confidence-Faithfulness Gap Meter. Problem: no simple tool jointly measures stated confidence and reasoning-answer consistency on the same items. Direction: collect answer, stated confidence, and a faithfulness signal per item; cross-tabulate to find high-confidence-but-fragile items; report the overconfident-and-unfaithful fraction as a gap metric.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain combining confidence + faithfulness signals; catastrophic-risk link remains a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Combines two known behavioral probes; inherited methods.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused single gap-metric; depends on two sub-probes.

novelty.reasoning: Gap concept introduced recently; combined turnkey meter may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The gap concept is published; a reusable combined meter is plausibly open.
